exposure: Birth tourism vs. non-birth tourism neonates
cohort: 46 birth tourism neonates admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) over 3 years, compared with 100 randomly selected non-birth tourism neonates
finding: Birth tourism neonates were more likely to be born to older women, via cesarean delivery, at a referral facility, and had longer hospital stays, more surgical intervention, and higher hospital charges.
mod_finding: Birth tourism neonates were more likely to be born via cesarean delivery (72% vs. 48%; p = 0.007).
